name: frankl_union_closed
claim_latex: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture (1979): for every finite union-closed family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets with $\mathcal{F} \neq \{\emptyset\}$, there exists an element $x$ belonging to at least half of the members of $\mathcal{F}$.

given_facts.statement: Gilmer (2022): there is a universal constant $c = 0.01$ such that in every finite union-closed family (not $\{\emptyset\}$) some element belongs to at least a $c$-fraction of the members.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: LOWER bound on the max element frequency — the first constant-fraction result, via an information-theoretic (entropy) argument. It does NOT prove the conjecture (which needs 1/2).
given_facts.citation: J. Gilmer, 'A constant lower bound for the union-closed sets conjecture', arXiv:2211.09055 (Nov 2022).
warns: F1 constrains counterexamples only weakly; F2 is the binding constraint.

given_facts.statement: Alweiss–Huang–Sellke (and independently others, days after Gilmer): the constant improves to $(3-\sqrt{5})/2 \approx 0.381966$; small further $\varepsilon$-improvements exist (Sawin, Pebody, Yu, Cambie line, roughly 0.3823).
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: LOWER bound on max element frequency. Any counterexample family must have its maximum frequency in the narrow window $[0.382, 0.5)$.
given_facts.citation: R. Alweiss, B. Huang, M. Sellke, arXiv:2211.11731, published Electron. J. Combin. 31(3) #P3.35 (2024); further improvements: Sawin, Pebody, Yu, Cambie (exact current record unverified, ~0.3823).
warns: The window [0.382, 0.5) is where any witness must live — max frequency strictly below half but necessarily at least ~0.382.

given_facts.statement: Chase–Lovett: $(3-\sqrt{5})/2$ is OPTIMAL for the 'approximate union-closed' relaxation — Gilmer-style entropy arguments alone cannot pass $\approx 0.382$.
given_facts.sign_disambiguation: A BARRIER result about a proof technique, not about the conjecture's truth. It does not say the conjecture is false or that 0.382 is the truth for exactly-union-closed families.
warns: A full proof must exploit exact union-closure beyond what the entropy relaxation sees; equally, a counterexample hunter should study the approximate-optimal families Chase–Lovett construct — they show what 'frequency just above 0.382' structures look like.

witness_schema.sets: list of lists of ints — the family members (distinct finite sets, elements are arbitrary ints, remapped internally). Caps: at most 5000 members, ground set at most 4096 elements, at most 500000 total element instances. The verifier checks union-closure exhaustively and requires EVERY element's frequency strictly below |F|/2.

status_audited: 2026-07-11 — full conjecture confirmed OPEN as of July 2026 (constant-fraction bounds known, see F1/F2). A 2025/2026 item titled 'An algorithmic proof of Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture' circulates but is not a recognized resolution.
note: Not an Erdős problem (Frankl 1979) but included in the Track 2 portfolio for its witness-decidable shape: a universal claim over finite objects where ONE verified finite family settles it. The verifier is fully polynomial (bitmask union-closure check, O(|F|^2) ORs) — no budget caveats, unlike erdos_gyarfas. Known small-case verifications mean a counterexample, if any, is large or structurally exotic; F2 forces its max frequency into [0.382, 0.5). Track 1-style search fits: evolve union-closed families (e.g. closures of random generators, lattice-derived families) minimizing max frequency, and keep the trajectory as evidence even when it plateaus above 0.5.
